grade.rationale: The module defines a concise, strongly discriminated message protocol and clear syntax-token types. No correctness or error-handling defects are evident in the supplied content; the only concern is inconsistent immutability in the token model.

summary: Well-structured type definitions with clear discriminated unions and appropriately narrow literal types. Immutability is only partially expressed, allowing token data to be mutated despite TokenLine being readonly. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied, and ESLint evidence was unavailable due to a missing dependency.

grade.rationale: The request and response variants are coherent, discriminated by kind, and consistently carry requestId for correlation. No correctness defect is apparent.
Names and unions are compact and easy to extend, though the partially readonly token representation makes ownership and mutation expectations less clear.
The constants, language vocabulary, token vocabulary, and protocol messages are plainly named and readily understandable.

Failures are represented as an explicit discriminated response carrying both request identity and a message. More structured error metadata could be added later if consumers require it, but its absence is not a demonstrated defect.
The pure data contracts are straightforward to instantiate and assert in tests. Coverage remains unknown, and mutable nested token data could permit unintended test-fixture changes.

findings.title: Token immutability is expressed inconsistently
findings.description: TokenLine prevents replacement of array elements, but each TokenSpan remains mutable, and chunk responses expose a mutable lines array. Consumers can therefore alter token text, kinds, or the chunk collection even though the readonly TokenLine alias suggests tokenization results are intended to be immutable. This weakens the contract and can allow accidental shared-state mutations in consumers and tests.
findings.recommendation: Make TokenSpan fields readonly and expose chunk lines as a readonly array, for example `readonly text`, `readonly kind`, and `lines: readonly TokenLine[]`. Apply the same convention consistently to other protocol fields if immutable message values are intended.
